hints: Write down the net gain charge[i] − drain[i] at each point. If the total over the whole loop is negative, can any start work? And when can a particular start fail?

Use prefix sums of net gain. Start j works exactly when no prefix sum after it (going around once) dips below the prefix sum at j. A suffix-min array (for the part before wrapping) and a prefix-min array (for the wrapped part, plus the total) let you test every start in O(1).

1. p[k] = sum of (charge − drain) for points 0..k−1; total = p[n].
  2. sufMin[j] = min of p[j+1..n]; preMin[j] = min of p[1..j].
  3. For j = 0, 1, …: start j works if p[j] ≤ sufMin[j] and (j == 0 or p[j] ≤ total + preMin[j]).
  4. Return the first j that works, else −1.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Simulate a full loop from every starting point.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Classic greedy: reset the start whenever the running balance goes negative. It finds A valid start, but when several work it may not be the smallest one.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Prefix sums with prefix-min and suffix-min arrays to test each start in O(1), returning the smallest valid start.

explain: Sample 1: net = [−1,−1,−1,4,−1], prefix p = [0,−1,−2,−3,1,0], total 0. For j = 3, p[3] = −3; later prefixes before wrapping are 1 and 0 (both ≥ −3), and wrapped prefixes are total + p[1..3] = −1,−2,−3 (all ≥ −3), so start 3 works. Starts 0,1,2 fail because a later prefix drops below theirs. Battery after riding from j to k equals p[k] − p[j], which is why 'never negative' becomes 'p[j] is a minimum over the next n prefixes'. Note that when the total is exactly 0 several starts can work, and we must return the smallest.
recognize: Circular route with gains and costs where the running total must stay non-negative → net-gain prefix sums (greedy reset or prefix minima).
